# Apache Virtual Host Without Domain Name

You can serve PHP projects directly via IP address without configuring a specific domain name, but you need to adjust your Apache configuration to treat those paths as distinct virtual hosts rather than relying on the default catch-all block. The core challenge lies in how Apache resolves requests when no `Host` header is provided or when the header matches a wildcard. By default, the `000-default.conf` file acts as a blanket catch-all, routing any request to `/var/www/html`. To serve `/projecta` and `/projectb` from their respective directories while keeping `/html/info.php` accessible, you must define specific virtual host blocks that intercept requests based on the URL path.

In your current setup, the `000-default.conf` file defines a generic VirtualHost listening on port 80 with `DocumentRoot` set to `/var/www/html`. When you visit `http://162.243.93.216/info.php`, Apache matches this request against the default configuration because no other rule claims it. The `<Directory>` directive inside this block grants access to `/var/www/`, which covers your subdirectories, but the routing logic remains tied to the single document root defined in the VirtualHost context.

To separate `projecta` and `projectb` into their own environments without domains, you need to create additional virtual host configurations that explicitly map the IP address and port to specific paths. You can achieve this by creating new configuration files in `/etc/apache2/sites-available/`, such as `projecta.conf` and `projectb.conf`.

Here is an example of how to configure the virtual host for `projecta`:

```apache
<VirtualHost *:80>
    ServerAdmin webmaster@localhost
    # Use a unique ServerName or leave it empty if relying on path-based routing
    ServerName 162.243.93.216
    
    # Explicitly set the document root for this specific project
    DocumentRoot /var/www/projecta

    <Directory /var/www/projecta>
        Options Indexes FollowSymLinks MultiViews
        AllowOverride All
        Require all granted
    </Directory>

    ErrorLog ${APACHE_LOG_DIR}/projecta-error.log
    CustomLog ${APACHE_LOG_DIR}/projecta-access.log combined
</VirtualHost>
```

However, simply adding this block might not be enough if Apache prioritizes the default `000-default.conf` for all requests or if your request handler still points to `/var/www/html`. The most robust approach when avoiding domain names is to use **Alias** directives or override the `DirectoryIndex` behavior, but a cleaner method for path-based separation without domains is to ensure the default virtual host only handles the root path (`/`) and lets specific VirtualHosts handle sub-paths if your web server supports them.

In modern Apache versions (2.4+), you can rely on `Location` directives within the default block or create separate blocks that take precedence based on the URL structure, though standard VirtualHost matching is primarily Host-header based. A more direct solution for path-based routing without domains involves using `Alias` in the main config or ensuring the default document root is restricted to `/html` while aliasing other paths.

Alternatively, you can configure the default virtual host to serve only the `/html` directory and use an `Alias` directive to map `/projecta` and `/projectb` to their actual directories:

```apache
# Inside /etc/apache2/sites-available/000-default.conf

<VirtualHost *:80>
    ServerAdmin webmaster@localhost
    DocumentRoot /var/www/html
    
    # Define the root location explicitly
    <Directory /var/www/html>
        Options Indexes FollowSymLinks MultiViews
        AllowOverride All
        Require all granted
    </Directory>

    # Map projecta to its directory
    Alias /projecta /var/www/projecta
    <Directory /var/www/projecta>
        Options Indexes FollowSymLinks MultiViews
        AllowOverride All
        Require all granted
    </Directory>

    # Map projectb to its directory
    Alias /projectb /var/www/projectb
    <Directory /var/www/projectb>
        Options Indexes FollowSymLinks MultiViews
        AllowOverride All
        Require all granted
    </Directory>

    ErrorLog ${APACHE_LOG_DIR}/error.log
    CustomLog ${APACHE_LOG_DIR}/access.log combined
</VirtualHost>
```

After editing the configuration files, you must test the syntax and restart the service to apply changes:

```bash
sudo apachectl configtest
sudo systemctl restart apache2
```

**Trade-offs and Considerations**

Using IP addresses directly with path-based routing is convenient for internal testing or simple setups but lacks the security and maintainability of domain names. Without a `ServerName`, Apache might log these requests under the IP address, making debugging harder. Additionally, if you ever decide to implement SSL (HTTPS), you will need certificates that match either the IP address or specific domains, which can be complex for bare IPs.

If you are managing multiple projects on a single VPS and want to keep them isolated, consider using containers or distinct document roots with proper aliasing. If your stack is Laravel-based or requires complex middleware configuration, ensure your `public` folders are correctly aliased. For instance, if `/projecta/public` contains the actual entry point, update the `Directory` permissions accordingly.

For production environments, always prefer domain names to leverage features like automatic SSL provisioning (e.g., Let's Encrypt via Certbot) and better DNS management. If you need further guidance on configuring Laravel-specific directories or optimizing Apache for high-traffic PHP applications, resources from [LaravelCompany](https://laravelcompany.com) can provide deeper insights into best practices for your specific stack.
